Code and data named on the slides, and used here

  • code/regression.py: the author’s script for the figure of p. 62. It runs Nadaraya–Watson with the kernel exp(γ x · y) for γ = 1 … 1000 on Lecture 2’s two toy datasets, and prints the mean |prediction − y| at the training points; the slide shows its output for γ = 50 (code/output_regression/2D_n100/attention_50.png, identical byte for byte to images/graph_learning/attention_2D.png). Under scikit-learn 1.9.1 it needs one change to run (its estimator must inherit from BaseEstimator); its printed numbers are then those of Lab 10. code/regression_2.py is an older copy of Lecture 2’s script.
  • Figures read for exact data: orientation/radial_filter.svg (p. 23; the same 9 × 9 grid as graph_learning/attention.svg), pooling/bottleneck.png (p. 25; 30 vertices and 82 edges digitised), gravity.png (p. 65; ten dots on a parabola to within 0.5 px), proteins/overview.svg (p. 46; the timings), mnist/mnist_results.png and robot/kitti_results.png (the tables of p. 35 and p. 55, transcribed), convolution/*.png (p. 11–18, identical to Lecture 1’s files).
  • Unused files in the lecture folder: pooling/oversquashing.png and curvature-000/002.png (Topping et al.’s rewiring), umap/DBSCAN BM20 viewed in UMAP.png, DBSCAN L07 viewed in UMAP.png and HSC_fr.png (the source of p. 6’s stem cells), sampling/intrinsic_2.png and intrinsic_triangulation.png, faust/faust_fake.png and shape0–9.jpg, mnist/mnist_graphs.png, proteins/masif_full.png, and a screenshot tracing Hinton’s portrait to WIRED.
  • Real data added on this page: MNIST (downloaded from the cvdf-datasets mirror, checksums as published; the page embeds the first 5,000 training images and every tenth test image at 4 grey levels, and ten test images at full resolution), the barnase–barstar complex from the Protein Data Bank (entry 1BRS, 864 + 693 heavy atoms, coordinates rounded to 0.01 Å), and the CT image of the convolution slides.

Reference implementations (Python)

Each script below runs with NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn, NetworkX, POT and umap-learn, and its output is shown under it. The page’s own code is independent JavaScript; the scripts use the libraries as references where they exist, and otherwise redo the page’s computation in Python. They use the page’s random generator (given first), so they reproduce the page’s random data exactly. Every number of the page’s findings is printed by one of these scripts, with three exceptions: umap-learn uses other random numbers than the page’s UMAP (79.3% against 79.1% purity), the supervised projection of scikit-learn differs slightly from the page’s (1-NN 86.7% against 86.8%), and the timings of Lab 5 depend on the computer.

0. The page’s random generator

"""The random generator of the companion pages (mulberry32 + Marsaglia's polar method), in Python.

The page's labs draw their random data with this generator; with the same seed, these functions return the
same numbers, so the snippets below reproduce the page's results instead of results "within sampling error".
"""
import math

M32 = 0xFFFFFFFF


def _imul(a, b):
    return (a * b) & M32


class Rng:
    def __init__(self, seed):
        self.a = (seed & M32) or 1
        self.spare = None

    def uniform(self):                       # uniform in [0, 1), bit-for-bit as the pages' G.rng(seed).uniform()
        self.a = (self.a + 0x6D2B79F5) & M32
        a = self.a
        t = _imul(a ^ (a >> 15), 1 | a)
        t = ((t + _imul(t ^ (t >> 7), 61 | t)) & M32) ^ t
        return ((t ^ (t >> 14)) & M32) / 4294967296

    def normal(self):                        # Marsaglia's polar method, keeping the spare value as the pages do
        if self.spare is not None:
            s0, self.spare = self.spare, None
            return s0
        while True:
            u, v = 2 * self.uniform() - 1, 2 * self.uniform() - 1
            s = u * u + v * v
            if 0 < s < 1:
                break
        f = math.sqrt(-2 * math.log(s) / s)
        self.spare = v * f
        return u * f

    def int(self, n):
        return math.floor(self.uniform() * n)

    def range(self, lo, hi):
        return lo + (hi - lo) * self.uniform()

    def normals(self, n):
        return [self.normal() for _ in range(n)]

    # ---- vectorised versions (same stream as repeated calls; used for millions of draws) ----
    def uniform_array(self, n):
        import numpy as np
        k = np.arange(1, n + 1, dtype=np.uint64)
        a = (np.uint64(self.a) + k * np.uint64(0x6D2B79F5)) & np.uint64(M32)
        self.a = int(a[-1]) if n else self.a
        m = np.uint64(M32)
        t = ((a ^ (a >> np.uint64(15))) * (a | np.uint64(1))) & m
        t = ((t + (((t ^ (t >> np.uint64(7))) * (t | np.uint64(61))) & m)) & m) ^ t
        return ((t ^ (t >> np.uint64(14))) & m).astype(np.float64) / 4294967296

    def normal_array(self, n):
        import numpy as np
        out = []
        if self.spare is not None and n > 0:
            out.append(self.spare); self.spare = None
        need = n - len(out)
        while need > 0:
            m = max(64, int(need * 0.66) + 64)             # pairs of uniforms to try
            u = self.uniform_array(2 * m)
            x, y = 2 * u[0::2] - 1, 2 * u[1::2] - 1
            s = x * x + y * y
            ok = (s < 1) & (s > 0)
            # keep the stream exact: stop at the pair that completes the request, rewind the rest
            idx = np.flatnonzero(ok)
            pairs_needed = (need + 1) // 2
            if len(idx) >= pairs_needed:
                last = int(idx[pairs_needed - 1])
                self.a = int((self.a - (2 * m - 2 * (last + 1)) * 0x6D2B79F5) & M32)
                idx = idx[:pairs_needed]
            f = np.sqrt(-2 * np.log(s[idx]) / s[idx])
            vals = np.empty(2 * len(idx)); vals[0::2] = x[idx] * f; vals[1::2] = y[idx] * f
            if len(vals) > need:
                self.spare = float(vals[-1]); vals = vals[:-1]
            out.extend(vals.tolist()); need -= len(vals)
        return np.array(out[:n])

1. Convolutions as message passing, isotropic filters (§1.2, Lab 1)

"""Lab 1 (p. 11-23): a convolution is message passing with the offset as edge feature; isotropic filters cannot see edges."""
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
from scipy.ndimage import correlate

x = np.asarray(Image.open("../../Lecture_4_deep_learning/images/convolution/filtered_1.png").convert("L"), float)   # 54 x 54
def norm(k): k = np.array(k, float).reshape(5, 5); return k / k.sum()
def deriv(p, n): k = np.zeros((5, 5)); k[p] = 1; k[n] = -1; return k
ident = np.zeros((5, 5)); ident[2, 2] = 1
filters = {"identity": ident,                                                   # the eight filters recovered in Lecture 1
  "cross blur": norm([0,0,0,0,0, 0,0,.5,0,0, 0,.5,1,.5,0, 0,0,.5,0,0, 0,0,0,0,0]),
  "bell blur": norm([0,.1,.2,.1,0, .1,.3,.5,.2,.1, .2,.5,1,.5,.2, .1,.3,.5,.3,.1, 0,.1,.2,.1,0]),
  "disc blur": norm([0,.7,.8,.7,0, .7,1,1,1,.7, .8,1,1,1,.8, .7,1,1,1,.7, 0,.7,.8,.7,0]),
  "horizontal derivative": deriv((2, 3), (2, 1)), "vertical derivative": deriv((1, 2), (3, 2)), "diagonal derivative": deriv((1, 3), (3, 1))}

def conv(img, k):   # (phi * x)[i,j] = sum_ab phi[a,b] x[i-a, j-b], borders replicated: scipy's correlate with the flipped kernel
    return correlate(img, k[::-1, ::-1], mode="nearest")
def message_passing(img, k):   # x'[i] = sum over the 25 neighbours k of phi(edge[i,k]) x[k], edge = offset
    h, w = img.shape; out = np.zeros_like(img)
    for a in range(-2, 3):
        for b in range(-2, 3):
            if k[a + 2, b + 2]: out += k[a + 2, b + 2] * img[np.clip(np.arange(h)[:, None] - a, 0, h - 1), np.clip(np.arange(w)[None, :] - b, 0, w - 1)]
    return out
print("max |message passing - convolution| over the 7 distinct filters:", max(np.abs(message_passing(x, k) - conv(x, k)).max() for k in filters.values()))

def A(img):   # one layer of vanilla (isotropic) message passing: the sum of the 4 neighbours
    p = np.pad(img, 1, mode="edge"); return p[:-2, 1:-1] + p[2:, 1:-1] + p[1:-1, :-2] + p[1:-1, 2:]
def basis(img, family, L=0):
    if family == "poly":
        B = [img]; [B.append(A(B[-1])) for _ in range(L)]; return B
    cls = (lambda a, b: abs(a) + abs(b)) if family == "rings" else (lambda a, b: tuple(sorted((abs(a), abs(b)))))
    keys = sorted({cls(a, b) for a in range(-2, 3) for b in range(-2, 3)})
    return [conv(img, np.array([[1.0 if cls(a, b) == c else 0 for b in range(-2, 3)] for a in range(-2, 3)])) for c in keys]
def r2(B, t, m=6):
    X = np.stack([b[m:-m, m:-m].ravel() for b in B], 1); y = t[m:-m, m:-m].ravel()
    c, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(X, y, rcond=None); r = y - X @ c
    return 1 - r @ r / ((y - y.mean()) @ (y - y.mean()))
fams = [("poly", 1), ("poly", 2), ("poly", 4), ("poly", 8), ("rings", 0), ("d4", 0)]
print("R^2 of the best isotropic imitation:   1 layer  2 layers  4 layers  8 layers  rings(p.23)  symmetric 5x5")
for name, k in filters.items():
    t = conv(x, k)
    print(f"  {name:22s}", "  ".join(f"{r2(basis(x, f, L), t):.4f}" for f, L in fams))

w = [1 - 213 / 255, 1 - 170 / 255, 1 - 42 / 255, 1 - 193 / 255]      # the fills of radial_filter.svg at graph distance 0..3
ring = np.array([[w[abs(a) + abs(b)] if abs(a) + abs(b) <= 3 else 0 for b in range(-3, 4)] for a in range(-3, 4)])
def gap(k, m=6):
    a, b = conv(np.rot90(x), k), np.rot90(conv(x, k)); return np.abs(a - b)[m:-m, m:-m].max()
print(f"rotate-then-filter vs filter-then-rotate: ring filter {gap(ring):.1e}, horizontal derivative {gap(filters['horizontal derivative']):.0f}")

2. Zeros of vector fields on a sphere and a torus (§1.4, Lab 2)

"""Lab 2 (p. 23): zeros of tangent vector fields on a triangulated sphere and torus; their indices add up to V - E + F."""
import numpy as np
from gda_rng import Rng

def icosphere(level):
    t = (1 + 5 ** .5) / 2
    V = [[-1,t,0],[1,t,0],[-1,-t,0],[1,-t,0],[0,-1,t],[0,1,t],[0,-1,-t],[0,1,-t],[t,0,-1],[t,0,1],[-t,0,-1],[-t,0,1]]
    V = [list(np.array(v) / np.linalg.norm(v)) for v in V]
    F = [[0,11,5],[0,5,1],[0,1,7],[0,7,10],[0,10,11],[1,5,9],[5,11,4],[11,10,2],[10,7,6],[7,1,8],[3,9,4],[3,4,2],[3,2,6],[3,6,8],[3,8,9],[4,9,5],[2,4,11],[6,2,10],[8,6,7],[9,8,1]]
    for _ in range(level):
        mid, NF = {}, []
        def m(a, b):
            k = (min(a, b), max(a, b))
            if k not in mid:
                p = (np.array(V[a]) + np.array(V[b])) / 2; V.append(list(p / np.linalg.norm(p))); mid[k] = len(V) - 1
            return mid[k]
        for f in F:
            a, b, c = m(f[0], f[1]), m(f[1], f[2]), m(f[2], f[0]); NF += [[f[0], a, c], [f[1], b, a], [f[2], c, b], [a, b, c]]
        F = NF
    return np.array(V), np.array(F)
def torus(R=1.0, r=0.42, nu=96, nv=40):
    V = [[(R + r * np.cos(2*np.pi*j/nv)) * np.cos(2*np.pi*i/nu), (R + r * np.cos(2*np.pi*j/nv)) * np.sin(2*np.pi*i/nu), r * np.sin(2*np.pi*j/nv)] for j in range(nv) for i in range(nu)]
    idx = lambda a, b: (b % nv) * nu + (a % nu); F = []
    for j in range(nv):
        for i in range(nu): F += [[idx(i, j), idx(i+1, j), idx(i+1, j+1)], [idx(i, j), idx(i+1, j+1), idx(i, j+1)]]
    return np.array(V), np.array(F)
def euler(V, F):
    E = {tuple(sorted((f[k], f[(k+1) % 3]))) for f in F for k in range(3)}; return len(V) - len(E) + len(F)
unit = lambda v: v / np.linalg.norm(v)
a = unit(np.array([0.3, 0.5, 0.81])); b = unit(np.cross(a, [1, 0, 0]))
tang = lambda v, n: v - (v @ n) * n
surf = {"sphere": (lambda p: unit(p), lambda p: unit(p)),
        "torus": (lambda p: unit(p - np.array([np.cos(np.arctan2(p[1], p[0])), np.sin(np.arctan2(p[1], p[0])), 0])),
                  lambda p: (lambda c: c + 0.42 * unit(p - c))(np.array([np.cos(np.arctan2(p[1], p[0])), np.sin(np.arctan2(p[1], p[0])), 0])))}
def dmonos(p):   # gradients of x, y, z, x^2, y^2, z^2, xy, yz, zx, x^3, y^3, z^3, xyz, x^2 y, y^2 z, z^2 x
    x, y, z = p
    return np.array([[1,0,0],[0,1,0],[0,0,1],[2*x,0,0],[0,2*y,0],[0,0,2*z],[y,x,0],[0,z,y],[z,0,x],[3*x*x,0,0],[0,3*y*y,0],[0,0,3*z*z],[y*z,x*z,x*y],[2*x*y,x*x,0],[0,2*y*z,y*y],[z*z,0,2*z*x]])
def field(s, kind, seed=1):
    normal = surf[s][0]
    if kind == "rotation": return lambda p: np.cross(a, p)
    if kind == "gradient" and s == "sphere": return lambda p: tang(a, p)
    if kind == "dipole":
        def f(p):
            pn = p @ a; u = (p - pn * a) / (1 - pn); uu, ua = u @ u, u @ b; D = uu + 1
            return ((2 * b + 2 * ua * a) * D - (2 * u + (uu - 1) * a) * 2 * ua) / D ** 2
        return f
    if kind == "combed": return lambda p: np.array([-np.sin(np.arctan2(p[1], p[0])), np.cos(np.arctan2(p[1], p[0])), 0])
    if kind == "gradient": d = unit(np.array([1, 0.13, 0.07])); return lambda p: tang(d, normal(p))
    r = Rng(seed); phi = np.array([r.normal() for _ in range(16)]); psi = np.array([r.normal() for _ in range(16)])   # the page's coefficients
    return lambda p: tang(phi @ dmonos(p), normal(p)) + np.cross(normal(p), psi @ dmonos(p))
def zeros(s, fld, S=6):
    V, F = MESH[s]; proj = surf[s][1]; out = []
    for fi, f in enumerate(F):
        P = V[f]; n = unit(np.cross(P[1] - P[0], P[2] - P[0])); vs = []
        for e in range(3):
            for k in range(S):
                t = k / S; v = fld(proj((1 - t) * P[e] + t * P[(e + 1) % 3])); vs.append(v - (v @ n) * n)
        tot = sum(np.arctan2(n @ np.cross(vs[k], vs[(k + 1) % len(vs)]), vs[k] @ vs[(k + 1) % len(vs)]) for k in range(len(vs)))
        w = int(round(tot / (2 * np.pi)))
        if w: out.append(w)
    return out
MESH = {"sphere": icosphere(4), "torus": torus()}
for s, kinds in [("sphere", ["rotation", "gradient", "dipole", "random"]), ("torus", ["combed", "gradient", "random"])]:
    V, F = MESH[s]; print(f"{s}: V = {len(V)}, F = {len(F)}, V - E + F = {euler(V, F)}")
    for k in kinds:
        z = zeros(s, field(s, k)); print(f"  {k:9s} zeros {len(z):2d}  indices {z}  sum {sum(z)}")
    counts = [len(zeros(s, field(s, "random", seed))) for seed in range(1, 21)]
    sums = {sum(zeros(s, field(s, "random", seed))) for seed in range(1, 21)}
    print(f"  20 random fields: zeros per field {min(counts)}-{max(counts)}, sums of indices {sums}")

  gradient  zeros  2  indices [1, 1]  sum 2
  dipole    zeros  1  indices [2]  sum 2

  20 random fields: zeros per field 2-8, sums of indices {2}
torus: V = 3840, F = 7680, V - E + F = 0

  gradient  zeros  4  indices [1, -1, -1, 1]  sum 0

3. Heat on three meshes (§1.5, Lab 3)

"""Lab 3 (p. 24): heat diffusion on one flat square meshed three ways: cotangent Laplacian vs mean over the neighbours."""
import numpy as np, scipy.sparse as sp, scipy.sparse.linalg as spl
from gda_rng import Rng

h, s0, t, steps = 0.04, 0.08, 0.01, 50
def lattice():
    dy = h * 3 ** .5 / 2; J = int(0.9 // dy); V, rows, F = [], [], []
    for j in range(-J, J + 1):
        off = h / 2 if abs(j) % 2 else 0; ids = []; x = -1 + off
        while x <= 1 + 1e-9: ids.append(len(V)); V.append([x, j * dy]); x += h
        rows.append((off, ids))
    for r in range(len(rows) - 1):
        (off, A), (_, B) = rows[r], rows[r + 1]
        if off == 0:
            for i in range(len(A) - 1):
                if i < len(B): F.append([A[i], A[i + 1], B[i]])
                if i + 1 < len(B): F.append([A[i + 1], B[i + 1], B[i]])
        else:
            for i in range(len(A)):
                if i + 1 < len(B): F.append([A[i], B[i + 1], B[i]])
                if i + 1 < len(A) and i + 1 < len(B): F.append([A[i], A[i + 1], B[i + 1]])
    return np.array(V), np.array(F)
V0, F = lattice()
xs = np.linspace(-1, 1, 4001); spc = np.exp(np.log(2) * np.tanh(xs / 0.35))
cum = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum((spc[1:] + spc[:-1]) / 2 * np.diff(xs))]); cum = cum / cum[-1] * 2 - 1
def warp(x):   # the page's piecewise-linear interpolation of the cumulative spacing
    u = (x + 1) / 2 * 4000; i = np.clip(np.floor(u).astype(int), 0, 3999); f = u - i
    return cum[i] * (1 - f) + cum[i + 1] * f
graded = np.c_[warp(V0[:, 0]), V0[:, 1]]
rng, ymax, jit = Rng(44), V0[:, 1].max(), V0.copy()
for i, p in enumerate(V0):
    if abs(p[0]) > 1 - 1e-6 or abs(p[1]) > ymax - 1e-6: continue          # the boundary stays in place
    ang = 2 * np.pi * rng.uniform(); rad = 0.3 * h * np.sqrt(rng.uniform()); jit[i] = p + rad * np.array([np.cos(ang), np.sin(ang)])
def cotan(P):
    I, J, W = [], [], []; M = np.zeros(len(P))
    for f in F:
        for c in range(3):
            a, b, o = f[c], f[(c + 1) % 3], f[(c + 2) % 3]; u, v = P[a] - P[o], P[b] - P[o]
            w = 0.5 * (u @ v) / abs(u[0] * v[1] - u[1] * v[0]); I += [a, b, a, b]; J += [b, a, a, b]; W += [-w, -w, w, w]
        M[f] += abs(np.cross(np.r_[P[f[1]] - P[f[0]], 0], np.r_[P[f[2]] - P[f[0]], 0])[2]) / 6
    return sp.csr_matrix((W, (I, J)), shape=(len(P), len(P))), M
bump = lambda P: np.exp(-(P ** 2).sum(1) / (2 * s0 ** 2))
exact = lambda P: s0 ** 2 / (s0 ** 2 + 2 * t) * np.exp(-(P ** 2).sum(1) / (2 * (s0 ** 2 + 2 * t)))
E = {tuple(sorted((f[c], f[(c + 1) % 3]))) for f in F for c in range(3)}
Adj = sp.csr_matrix((np.ones(2 * len(E)), (np.r_[[e[0] for e in E], [e[1] for e in E]], np.r_[[e[1] for e in E], [e[0] for e in E]])), shape=(len(V0), len(V0)))
deg = np.asarray(Adj.sum(1)).ravel(); K = round(4 * t / (0.5 * h * h))
def stats(P, u, M):
    w = M * u; cx = (w * P[:, 0]).sum() / w.sum(); sx = np.sqrt((w * (P[:, 0] - cx) ** 2).sum() / w.sum()); cy = (w * P[:, 1]).sum() / w.sum()
    sy = np.sqrt((w * (P[:, 1] - cy) ** 2).sum() / w.sum()); inner = (np.abs(P) < 0.6).all(1)
    err = np.sqrt((M * (u - exact(P)) ** 2)[inner].sum() / M[inner].sum()) / exact(np.zeros((1, 2)))[0]
    return f"centre x {cx:+.4f}  spread x {sx:.4f}  y {sy:.4f}  error {100 * err:.2f}%"
print(f"{len(V0)} vertices, {len(F)} triangles; {K} message-passing steps (tau = 0.5); {steps} implicit Euler steps")
for name, P in [("uniform", V0), ("graded", graded), ("jittered", jit)]:
    L, M = cotan(P); A = (sp.diags(M) + (t / steps) * L).tocsc(); u = bump(P)
    for _ in range(steps): u = spl.spsolve(A, M * u)
    v = bump(P)
    for _ in range(K): v = v + 0.5 * (Adj @ v / deg - v)
    print(f"{name:9s} cotangent + mass: {stats(P, u, M)}\n{'':9s} mean over neighbours: {stats(P, v, M)}")

4. Curvature, over-squashing, rewiring and pooling (§1.6, Lab 4)

"""Lab 4 (p. 21, 25): curvature of the bottleneck graph, over-squashing of a linear GCN, rewiring, and pooling (networkx + POT)."""
import json, numpy as np, networkx as nx, ot

d = json.load(open("../lecture4/assets/l4data.json"))["bottleneck"]          # 30 vertices, 82 edges digitised from bottleneck.png
def graph(extra=()):
    g = nx.Graph(); g.add_nodes_from(range(len(d["xy"]))); g.add_edges_from(map(tuple, d["edges"])); g.add_edges_from(extra); return g
def orc(g, u, v):   # Ollivier-Ricci curvature, uniform measures on the closed neighbourhoods, exact OT (POT)
    Nu, Nv = [u] + sorted(g[u]), [v] + sorted(g[v]); D = dict(nx.all_pairs_shortest_path_length(g)) if not hasattr(g, "_D") else g._D
    C = np.array([[D[x][y] for y in Nv] for x in Nu], float)
    return 1 - ot.emd2(np.full(len(Nu), 1 / len(Nu)), np.full(len(Nv), 1 / len(Nv)), C)
def curvatures(g):
    g._D = dict(nx.all_pairs_shortest_path_length(g)); return {tuple(sorted(e)): orc(g, *e) for e in g.edges}
g0 = graph(); bridge = list(nx.bridges(g0)); h = g0.copy(); h.remove_edges_from(bridge)
label = {v: k for k, comp in enumerate(nx.connected_components(h)) for v in comp}
K = curvatures(g0); vals = sorted(K.values())
print(f"{g0.number_of_nodes()} vertices, {g0.number_of_edges()} edges, bridge {bridge}, clusters of {sorted(map(len, nx.connected_components(h)))}")
print(f"curvature: bridge {K[tuple(sorted(bridge[0]))]:.3f}, next {vals[1]:.3f}, median {np.median(vals):.3f}, negative edges {sum(v < 0 for v in vals)}")
def sensitivity(g, L):   # mean (A_hat^L)_ij across the bridge and within the clusters, A_hat = D^-1/2 (A + I) D^-1/2
    n = g.number_of_nodes(); A = nx.to_numpy_array(g, nodelist=range(n)) + np.eye(n); dg = A.sum(1)
    P = np.linalg.matrix_power(A / np.sqrt(np.outer(dg, dg)), L); lab = np.array([label[i] for i in range(n)]); off = ~np.eye(n, dtype=bool)
    same = (lab[:, None] == lab[None, :]) & off; cross = lab[:, None] != lab[None, :]
    return P[cross].mean(), P[same].mean()
for L in (1, 4, 8):
    c, w = sensitivity(g0, L); print(f"L = {L}: across {c:.2e}, within {w:.2e}, ratio {w / c:.1f}")
added, g = [], g0                                   # rewiring: add the edge that raises the most negative curvature the most
for step in range(6):
    K = curvatures(g); (i, j) = min(K, key=lambda e: (K[e], e))
    best, bk = None, -np.inf
    for k in sorted([i] + list(g[i])):
        for l in sorted([j] + list(g[j])):
            if k == l or g.has_edge(k, l): continue
            t = graph(added + [(min(k, l), max(k, l))]); t._D = dict(nx.all_pairs_shortest_path_length(t)); kk = orc(t, i, j)
            if kk > bk + 1e-12: bk, best = kk, (min(k, l), max(k, l))
    added.append(best); g = graph(added)
K = curvatures(g); c, w = sensitivity(g, 4)
print(f"after adding {added}: most negative curvature {min(K.values()):.3f}, diameter {nx.diameter(g)} (was {nx.diameter(g0)}), "
      f"L = 4 across {c:.2e}, ratio {w / c:.1f}")
def coarsen(g):   # heavy-edge matching in index order, weight 1/deg(u) + 1/deg(v)
    match = {}
    for i in sorted(g):
        if i in match: continue
        cand = [(1 / g.degree(i) + 1 / g.degree(j), -j) for j in g[i] if j not in match]
        if cand: j = -max(cand)[1]; match[i], match[j] = j, i
        else: match[i] = i
    new, m = {}, 0
    for i in sorted(g):
        if i not in new: new[i] = m; new[match[i]] = m; m += 1
    return nx.Graph([(new[a], new[b]) for a, b in g.edges if new[a] != new[b]]) if m > 1 else nx.empty_graph(1)
for name, g in [("8x8 grid", nx.convert_node_labels_to_integers(nx.grid_2d_graph(8, 8), ordering="sorted")), ("clique of 10", nx.complete_graph(10)), ("bottleneck", g0)]:
    levels = [g]
    for _ in range(4): levels.append(coarsen(levels[-1]))
    print(f"pooling {name:12s}: " + " -> ".join(f"{x.number_of_nodes()}v/d{nx.diameter(x) if x.number_of_nodes() > 1 else 0}" for x in levels))

5. Memory transactions and cache misses (§1.7, Lab 5)

"""Lab 5 (p. 26): memory transactions of a gather on a GPU (warps of 32 threads, 32-byte sectors) and misses of a CPU cache."""
import numpy as np
from collections import OrderedDict
from scipy.spatial import cKDTree
from gda_rng import Rng

def csr(nbrs, sort=True):            # each vertex: itself first, then its neighbours (in increasing order for the K-NN graph)
    ptr = np.zeros(len(nbrs) + 1, int); ptr[1:] = np.cumsum([len(x) + 1 for x in nbrs])
    col = np.concatenate([[i] + (sorted(x) if sort else list(x)) for i, x in enumerate(nbrs)]); return ptr, col
n = 256; N = n * n
r, c = np.divmod(np.arange(N), n)
grid = csr([[((r[i] - 1) % n) * n + c[i], ((r[i] + 1) % n) * n + c[i], r[i] * n + (c[i] - 1) % n, r[i] * n + (c[i] + 1) % n] for i in range(N)], sort=False)   # up, down, left, right
grid_pos = np.c_[c, r] / n
pos = Rng(5).uniform_array(2 * N).reshape(N, 2)             # the page's random points (x, y interleaved)
_, idx = cKDTree(pos).query(pos, k=7)
nb = [set() for _ in range(N)]
for i in range(N):
    for j in idx[i, 1:]: nb[i].add(int(j)); nb[int(j)].add(i)
knn = csr([list(s) for s in nb]); knn_pos = pos
def order(kind, p):
    o = np.arange(N)
    if kind == "random":
        rg = Rng(123)
        for i in range(N - 1, 0, -1):
            j = int(rg.uniform() * (i + 1)); o[i], o[j] = o[j], o[i]
    elif kind == "morton":
        q = np.minimum(65535, np.floor(p * 65536).astype(np.int64)); key = np.zeros(N, np.int64)
        for b in range(15, -1, -1): key = key * 4 + ((q[:, 1] >> b) & 1) * 2 + ((q[:, 0] >> b) & 1)
        o = np.lexsort((np.arange(N), key))
    return o
def relabel(g, o):
    ptr, col = g; newpos = np.empty(N, int); newpos[o] = np.arange(N)
    rows = [newpos[col[ptr[v]:ptr[v + 1]]] for v in o]; return csr_from_rows(rows)
def csr_from_rows(rows):
    ptr = np.zeros(len(rows) + 1, int); ptr[1:] = np.cumsum([len(x) for x in rows]); return ptr, np.concatenate(rows)
def warp_stats(g, C):
    ptr, col = g; deg = np.diff(ptr); D = deg.max(); M = -np.ones((N, D), np.int64)
    for s in range(D): ok = deg > s; M[ok, s] = col[ptr[:-1][ok] + s]
    W = M.reshape(-1, 32, D); sectors = ideal = 0; b = 4 * C
    for s in range(D):
        v = W[:, :, s]; act = v >= 0
        lo, hi = np.where(act, v * b // 32, -1), np.where(act, (v * b + b - 1) // 32, -1)
        S = np.sort(np.concatenate([lo, hi], 1), 1); newv = np.diff(S, axis=1) != 0
        sectors += int(((S[:, 1:] >= 0) & newv).sum() + (S[:, 0] >= 0).sum()); ideal += int(np.ceil(act.sum(1) * b / 32).sum())
    maxd = deg.reshape(-1, 32).max(1); eff = deg.sum() / (32 * maxd).sum()
    return sectors / ideal, eff
def cache_misses(g, lines=512, per=16):
    ptr, col = g; lru, miss = OrderedDict(), 0
    for line in (col // per).tolist():
        if line in lru: lru.move_to_end(line)
        else:
            miss += 1; lru[line] = 1
            if len(lru) > lines: lru.popitem(last=False)
    return miss / len(col)
for name, g, p in [("grid 256x256", grid, grid_pos), ("K-NN of random points", knn, knn_pos)]:
    print(f"{name}: degrees (with the vertex itself) {np.diff(g[0]).min()}-{np.diff(g[0]).max()}")
    for kind in ["natural", "random", "morton"]:
        h = relabel(g, order(kind, p)); rs = [warp_stats(h, C) for C in (1, 2, 4, 8, 16)]
        print(f"  {kind:8s} sectors / ideal for 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 floats: " + " ".join(f"{x[0]:.2f}" for x in rs) + f"; warp efficiency {100 * rs[0][1]:.1f}%; cache misses {100 * cache_misses(h):.1f}%")

6. Nearest-neighbour votes on MNIST (§1.9, Lab 6)

"""Lab 6 (p. 35): nearest-neighbour votes on MNIST: the full data, the page's subset, and superpixel images.
MNIST from storage.googleapis.com/cvdf-datasets/mnist (the four .gz files, md5-checked), in ../lecture4/data."""
import gzip, os, numpy as np

D = "../lecture4/data"
def idx(name):
    b = gzip.open(os.path.join(D, name)).read()
    return np.frombuffer(b, np.uint8, offset=16).reshape(-1, 784) if b[3] == 3 else np.frombuffer(b, np.uint8, offset=8)
Xtr, ytr, Xte, yte = (idx(f) for f in ["train-images-idx3-ubyte.gz", "train-labels-idx1-ubyte.gz", "t10k-images-idx3-ubyte.gz", "t10k-labels-idx1-ubyte.gz"])
def neighbours(A, B, K, chunk=500):   # K nearest training rows for each test row: smallest (distance, index), exact integer distances
    A = A.astype(np.int64); nA = (A * A).sum(1); out = []
    for s in range(0, len(B), chunk):
        Bc = B[s:s + chunk].astype(np.int64); Dm = (Bc * Bc).sum(1)[:, None] + nA[None] - 2 * Bc @ A.T
        kth = np.partition(Dm, K - 1, 1)[:, K - 1]                   # ties at the K-th distance: keep the lowest indices
        for dm, t in zip(Dm, kth):
            c = np.flatnonzero(dm <= t); out.append(c[np.lexsort((c, dm[c]))][:K])
    return np.array(out)
def vote(nn, ytrain, K): return np.array([np.bincount(ytrain[r[:K]], minlength=10).argmax() for r in nn])
nn = neighbours(Xtr, Xte, 5)
print("full MNIST (60,000 / 10,000, 256 grey levels): " + ", ".join(f"{K}-NN {100 * (vote(nn, ytr, K) == yte).mean():.2f}%" for K in (1, 3, 5)))
te = np.arange(0, 10000, 10)                                       # the page: every 10th test image, first 5,000 training images
q = lambda A: np.minimum((A.astype(int) * 4) // 256, 3)            # 4 grey levels (2 bits per pixel)
NS = [50, 100, 200, 300, 500, 1000, 2000, 3000, 5000]
for K in (1, 3, 5):
    accs = [100 * (vote(neighbours(q(Xtr[:n]), q(Xte[te]), K), ytr, K) == yte[te]).mean() for n in NS]
    print(f"page subset, 4 grey levels, {K}-NN, n = " + " ".join(f"{n}:{a:.1f}" for n, a in zip(NS, accs)))
nn8 = neighbours(Xtr[:5000], Xte[te], 1)
print(f"same subset with 256 grey levels, 1-NN, n = 5000: {100 * (ytr[nn8[:, 0]] == yte[te]).mean():.1f}%")

def slic(img, grid=9, m=0.3, iters=6):   # the page's superpixels: k-means on (x/S, y/S, v/m) from a 9 x 9 grid of seeds, 2S windows
    S = 28 / grid; g = (np.arange(grid) + 0.5) * S; cy, cx = [a.ravel() for a in np.meshgrid(g, g, indexing="ij")]
    cv = img[np.minimum(27, np.floor(cy).astype(int)) * 28 + np.minimum(27, np.floor(cx).astype(int))].astype(float)
    x = np.arange(784) % 28 + 0.5; y = np.arange(784) // 28 + 0.5
    for _ in range(iters):
        Dd = ((x[:, None] - cx) ** 2 + (y[:, None] - cy) ** 2) / S ** 2 + (img[:, None] - cv) ** 2 / m ** 2
        Dd[(np.abs(x[:, None] - cx) > 2 * S) | (np.abs(y[:, None] - cy) > 2 * S)] = np.inf
        lab = Dd.argmin(1)
        for k in range(grid * grid):
            s = lab == k
            if s.any(): cx[k], cy[k], cv[k] = x[s].mean(), y[s].mean(), img[s].mean()
    return cv[lab]
R = np.array([slic((q(im) + 0.5) / 4) for im in np.concatenate([Xtr[:5000], Xte[te]])], np.float32).astype(np.float64)
A, B = R[:5000], R[5000:]
best = np.array([np.lexsort((np.arange(5000), ((A - b) ** 2).sum(1)))[0] for b in B])
print(f"superpixel images (81 regions), 1-NN, n = 5000: {100 * (ytr[best] == yte[te]).mean():.1f}%")

7. A protein surface after dMaSIF (§2.1, Lab 7)

"""Lab 7 (p. 41-46): the surface of barnase (PDB 1BRS, chain A) from its atoms, after dMaSIF, with the page's random samples;
curvatures at several scales, the rotation test, and the curvature of facing points on barstar (chain D)."""
import numpy as np
from scipy.spatial import cKDTree
from gda_rng import Rng

RAD = {"C": 1.70, "N": 1.55, "O": 1.52, "S": 1.80}
def atoms(chain):   # heavy atoms, first alternate location only
    X, E = [], []
    for l in open("../lecture4/data/1BRS.pdb"):
        if l.startswith("ATOM") and l[21] == chain and l[16] in " A" and (l[76:78].strip() or l[12:14].strip()) != "H":
            X.append([float(l[30:38]), float(l[38:46]), float(l[46:54])]); E.append(l[76:78].strip())
    return np.round(np.array(X) * 100) / 100, E                       # the page stores coordinates in hundredths of an angstrom
T, SMOOTH, B, NITS, RES = 1.05, 0.5, 20, 4, 1.0
def soft_distance(A, sig, tree, p):
    idx = tree.query_ball_point(p, 10.0)
    if not idx: idx = list(tree.query(p, 8)[1])
    idx = np.array(idx); v = p - A[idx]; d = np.linalg.norm(v, axis=1); u = v / d[:, None]; s = sig[idx]
    e = -d / s; m = e.max(); w = np.exp(e - m); S1 = w.sum(); L = np.log(S1) + m; pw = w / S1
    q = np.exp(-d - (-d).max()); q /= q.sum(); sb = (q * s).sum()
    return -sb * L, L * ((q * (s - sb))[:, None] * u).sum(0) + sb * ((pw / s)[:, None] * u).sum(0)
def surface(A, E, seed):
    sig = np.array([SMOOTH * RAD[e] / 1.10 for e in E]); tree = cKDTree(A); r = Rng(seed)
    Z = np.array([[A[i, 0] + 10 * T * r.normal(), A[i, 1] + 10 * T * r.normal(), A[i, 2] + 10 * T * r.normal()] for i in range(len(A)) for _ in range(B)])
    for _ in range(NITS):                                              # gradient steps on (SD - T)^2 / 2
        for k in range(len(Z)): s, g = soft_distance(A, sig, tree, Z[k]); Z[k] = Z[k] - (s - T) * g
    keep = np.array([abs(soft_distance(A, sig, tree, z)[0] - T) < 0.1 * T for z in Z]); ZZ = Z.copy()
    for _ in range(NITS):                                              # push outwards: points trapped inside stay close to the atoms
        for k in np.flatnonzero(keep): g = soft_distance(A, sig, tree, ZZ[k])[1]; ZZ[k] += T * g / np.linalg.norm(g)
    keep &= np.array([soft_distance(A, sig, tree, z)[0] > 1.5 * T if kk else False for z, kk in zip(ZZ, keep)])
    cells = {}
    for z in Z[keep]: cells.setdefault(tuple(np.floor(z / RES).astype(int)), []).append(z)
    P = np.array([np.mean(v, 0) for v in cells.values()])
    N = np.array([(lambda g: g / np.linalg.norm(g))(soft_distance(A, sig, tree, p)[1]) for p in P])
    return P - 0.5 * N, N, len(Z), int(keep.sum())
def frame(n):
    s = 1.0 if n[2] >= 0 else -1.0; a = -1 / (s + n[2]); b = n[0] * n[1] * a
    return np.array([1 + s * n[0] ** 2 * a, s * b, -s * n[0]]), np.array([b, s + n[1] ** 2 * a, -n[1]])
def curvatures(P, N, s, reg=0.01):
    tree = cKDTree(P); nb = tree.query_ball_point(P, 4 * s); Ns = np.zeros_like(N)
    for i, idx in enumerate(nb):
        w = np.exp(-((P[idx] - P[i]) ** 2).sum(1) / (2 * s * s)); v = (w[:, None] * N[idx]).sum(0); Ns[i] = v / np.linalg.norm(v)
    H, K = np.zeros(len(P)), np.zeros(len(P))
    for i, idx in enumerate(nb):
        u, v = frame(Ns[i]); dx = P[idx] - P[i]; dn = Ns[idx] - Ns[i]
        w = np.exp(-((dx ** 2).sum(1) * (2 - Ns[idx] @ Ns[i]) ** 2) / (2 * s * s))
        p = np.c_[dx @ u, dx @ v]; q = np.c_[dn @ u, dn @ v]
        Sm = np.linalg.solve((w[:, None, None] * p[:, :, None] * p[:, None, :]).sum(0) + reg * np.eye(2), (w[:, None, None] * p[:, :, None] * q[:, None, :]).sum(0))
        H[i] = np.clip(np.trace(Sm), -1, 1); K[i] = np.clip(np.linalg.det(Sm), -1, 1)
    return H, K
A, EA = atoms("A"); D, ED = atoms("D")
PA, NA, ns, kept = surface(A, EA, 1)
print(f"barnase: {len(A)} atoms, {kept} of {ns} samples kept, {len(PA)} surface points")
PD, ND, _, _ = surface(D, ED, 2); print(f"barstar: {len(D)} atoms, {len(PD)} surface points")
scales = [1, 2, 3, 5, 10]; CA = [curvatures(PA, NA, s) for s in scales]; CD = [curvatures(PD, ND, s) for s in scales]
print("share of positive H (convex) on barnase: " + ", ".join(f"{s} A {100 * (c[0] > 0).mean():.1f}%" for s, c in zip(scales, CA)))
print("barnase points with H <= 0 at 5 A and 10 A:", int((CA[3][0] <= 0).sum()), int((CA[4][0] <= 0).sum()))
dist, j = cKDTree(PD).query(PA); sel = dist < 2; r77 = Rng(77); perm = np.array([int(r77.uniform() * len(PD)) for _ in range(sel.sum())])
print(f"{sel.sum()} barnase points within 2 A of barstar; correlation of H with the facing point: " +
      ", ".join(f"{s} A {np.corrcoef(c[0][sel], d[0][j[sel]])[0, 1]:+.3f}" for s, c, d in zip(scales, CA, CD)))
print("  same with random barstar points: " + ", ".join(f"{s} A {np.corrcoef(c[0][sel], d[0][perm])[0, 1]:+.3f}" for s, c, d in zip(scales, CA, CD)))
w = np.array([0.9, -1.7, 0.4]); th = np.linalg.norm(w); k = w / th; Kx = np.array([[0, -k[2], k[1]], [k[2], 0, -k[0]], [-k[1], k[0], 0]])
R = np.eye(3) + np.sin(th) * Kx + (1 - np.cos(th)) * Kx @ Kx; t = np.array([12, -5, 30.0])

8. Registration by optimal transport (§2.3–2.4, Lab 8)

"""Lab 8 (p. 49-56): registering a deformed tree of vessels with nearest neighbours, optimal transport and robust (unbalanced)
optimal transport, with the page's random tree; Sinkhorn in the log domain with epsilon-scaling, checked against POT."""
import numpy as np, ot
from scipy.special import logsumexp
from gda_rng import Rng

def tree(seed=4, depth=6):
    r, segs = Rng(seed), []
    def rec(p, a, l, d):
        q = (p[0] + l * np.cos(a), p[1] + l * np.sin(a)); segs.append((p, q))
        if d < depth:
            da = 0.5 * (0.6 + 0.8 * r.uniform())
            rec(q, a + da, l * 0.72 * (0.85 + 0.3 * r.uniform()), d + 1); rec(q, a - da, l * 0.72 * (0.85 + 0.3 * r.uniform()), d + 1)
    rec((0.0, -0.9), np.pi / 2, 0.42, 0); return segs
def sample(segs, r, spacing=0.012, jitter=0.004):
    P = []
    for p, q in segs:
        p, q = np.array(p), np.array(q); L = np.linalg.norm(q - p); m = max(2, int(np.floor(L / spacing)))                   # as the page: floor(L / spacing), not L // spacing
        ts = sorted(r.uniform() for _ in range(m)); nrm = np.array([-(q - p)[1], (q - p)[0]]) / L
        for t in ts: P.append(p + t * (q - p) + jitter * r.normal() * nrm)
    return np.array(P)
def problem(partial, seed=4):
    segs, r = tree(seed), Rng(seed * 7 + 1)
    mu = [(-0.6 + 1.2 * r.uniform(), -0.6 + 1.2 * r.uniform()) for _ in range(6)]; amp = [(0.05 * r.normal(), 0.05 * r.normal()) for _ in range(6)]
    def phi(P):
        out = P * [1.04, 1.10] + [0.02, 0.05]
        for m, a in zip(mu, amp): out = out + np.outer(np.exp(-((P - m) ** 2).sum(1) / (2 * 0.25 ** 2)), a)
        return out
    X = sample(segs, r); Y0 = sample(segs, r); Y = phi(Y0)
    Y = Y + np.array([[0.003 * r.normal(), 0.003 * r.normal()] for _ in range(len(Y))])
    region = lambda P: (P[:, 0] > 0.15) & (P[:, 1] > 0.1)
    if partial:
        Y = Y[~region(Y0)]; k = round(0.1 * len(Y)); Y = np.vstack([Y, [[-1 + 2 * r.uniform(), -1 + 2 * r.uniform()] for _ in range(k)]])
    return X, Y, phi(X) - X, ~region(X) if partial else np.ones(len(X), bool)
def sinkhorn(X, Y, eps, rho=None, q=0.9, extra=20):   # the page's schedule: eps from max C down to eps (x 0.9 per step), then 20 more iterations
    C = ((X[:, None] - Y[None]) ** 2).sum(-1) / 2; la, lb = -np.log(len(X)) * np.ones(len(X)), -np.log(len(Y)) * np.ones(len(Y))
    f, g, e = np.zeros(len(X)), np.zeros(len(Y)), max(C.max(), eps)
    lam = lambda e: 1 if rho is None else rho / (rho + e)
    while True:
        f = -lam(e) * e * logsumexp((g[None] - C) / e + lb[None], axis=1); g = -lam(e) * e * logsumexp((f[:, None] - C) / e + la[:, None], axis=0)
        if e <= eps: break
        e = max(eps, e * q)
    for _ in range(extra):
        f = -lam(eps) * eps * logsumexp((g[None] - C) / eps + lb[None], axis=1); g = -lam(eps) * eps * logsumexp((f[:, None] - C) / eps + la[:, None], axis=0)
    return np.exp((f[:, None] + g[None] - C) / eps + la[:, None] + lb[None])
def barycentric(X, Y, P): m = P.sum(1); return (P @ Y) / m[:, None] - X, m
def smooth(X, V, w, s):
    K = w[None] * np.exp(-((X[:, None] - X[None]) ** 2).sum(-1) / (2 * s * s)); return (K @ V) / K.sum(1, keepdims=True)
EXTRA = 20                                                             # iterations at the final blur (the page: 20)
def prealign(X, Y):
    V, m = barycentric(X, Y, sinkhorn(X, Y, 0.05 ** 2, rho=0.1, extra=EXTRA)); w = np.sqrt(m)[:, None]
    M, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(np.c_[X, np.ones(len(X))] * w, (X + V) * w, rcond=None); return np.c_[X, np.ones(len(X))] @ M
def run(X, Y, method, pre, s):
    Xa = prealign(X, Y) if pre else X
    if method == "nn": V = Y[((Xa[:, None] - Y[None]) ** 2).sum(-1).argmin(1)] - Xa; m = np.ones(len(X))
    else: V, m = barycentric(Xa, Y, sinkhorn(Xa, Y, 0.02 ** 2, rho=0.1 if method == "rot" else None, extra=EXTRA))
    return Xa + (smooth(Xa, V, m, s) if s else V) - X
def metrics(V, Vt, mask):
    e = np.linalg.norm(V - Vt, axis=1)[mask]; rel = e / np.linalg.norm(Vt, axis=1)[mask]
    return f"EPE {e.mean():.4f}  AccS {100 * np.mean((e < 0.01) | (rel < 0.05)):5.1f}%  AccR {100 * np.mean((e < 0.02) | (rel < 0.1)):5.1f}%  outliers {100 * np.mean((e > 0.05) | (rel > 0.3)):5.1f}%"
ROWS = [("nn", 0, 0), ("nn", 0, .05), ("ot", 0, 0), ("ot", 0, .05), ("ot", 1, .05), ("rot", 1, 0), ("rot", 1, .05)]
for partial in (False, True):
    X, Y, Vt, mask = problem(partial)
    print(("partial target" if partial else "full target") + f": {len(X)} source points, {len(Y)} target points, mean true displacement {np.linalg.norm(Vt, axis=1).mean():.4f}")
    for method, pre, s in ROWS:
        print(f"  {method:3s} {'pre-aligned' if pre else '           '} smoothing {s:4}: {metrics(run(X, Y, method, pre, s), Vt, mask)}")
EXTRA = 3000                                                           # the same rows with (nearly) converged Sinkhorn iterations
print("with 3,000 iterations at the final blur instead of 20:")
for partial in (False, True):
    X, Y, Vt, mask = problem(partial)
    for method, pre, s in ROWS[2:]:
        print(f"  {'partial' if partial else 'full   '} {method:3s} {'pre-aligned' if pre else '           '} smoothing {s:4}: {metrics(run(X, Y, method, pre, s), Vt, mask)}")
X, Y, Vt, mask = problem(False)                                        # check against POT at the final blur
C = ((X[:, None] - Y[None]) ** 2).sum(-1) / 2; a, b = np.ones(len(X)) / len(X), np.ones(len(Y)) / len(Y)
Pp = ot.sinkhorn(a, b, C, reg=0.02 ** 2, method="sinkhorn_log", numItermax=5000, stopThr=1e-10)
Vp, _ = barycentric(X, Y, Pp); Po = sinkhorn(X, Y, 0.02 ** 2, extra=20); Vo, _ = barycentric(X, Y, Po)
print(f"balanced OT, the page's schedule: row-marginal error {np.abs(Po.sum(1) - a).sum():.1e}; POT, 5,000 log-domain iterations: {np.abs(Pp.sum(1) - a).sum():.1e}, "
      f"its flow {metrics(Vp, Vt, mask)}; largest difference between the two flows {np.abs(Vp - Vo).max():.3f}")
Pr = ot.unbalanced.sinkhorn_unbalanced(a, b, C, reg=0.02 ** 2, reg_m=0.1, method="sinkhorn", numItermax=20000, stopThr=1e-12)
Vr, _ = barycentric(X, Y, Pr); Pq = sinkhorn(X, Y, 0.02 ** 2, rho=0.1, extra=20); Vq, _ = barycentric(X, Y, Pq)
print(f"robust OT (reach 0.1): transported mass {Pq.sum():.3f} with the page's schedule, {Pr.sum():.3f} converged (POT); largest difference between the flows {np.abs(Vr - Vq).max():.3f}")

"""Lab 9 (p. 58-59): label purity of K-NN graphs of 1,000 MNIST images in six representations (scikit-learn, umap-learn)."""
import gzip, numpy as np
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
from sklearn.discriminant_analysis import LinearDiscriminantAnalysis
from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors
import umap

b = gzip.open("../lecture4/data/train-images-idx3-ubyte.gz").read(); Xall = np.frombuffer(b, np.uint8, offset=16).reshape(-1, 784)
yall = np.frombuffer(gzip.open("../lecture4/data/train-labels-idx1-ubyte.gz").read(), np.uint8, offset=8)
lev = np.minimum((Xall[:5000].astype(int) * 4) // 256, 3)              # the page's images: 4 grey levels
X = (lev + 0.5) * 64 / 255; N = 1000; y = yall[:N]
def purity_from_idx(idx, y): return (y[idx] == y[:, None]).mean()
def knn_idx(Z, K):   # K nearest (excluding the point itself), ties broken by index as on the page
    D = ((Z[:, None, :] - Z[None, :, :]) ** 2).sum(-1); np.fill_diagonal(D, np.inf)
    return np.array([np.lexsort((np.arange(len(Z)), d))[:K] for d in D])
def row(name, Z):
    print(f"  {name:48s} dim {Z.shape[1]:3d}  purity (10-NN) {100 * purity_from_idx(knn_idx(Z, 10), y):5.1f}%   1-NN {100 * purity_from_idx(knn_idx(Z, 1), y):5.1f}%")
counts = np.bincount(y, minlength=10); print(f"chance level: {100 * (counts * (counts - 1)).sum() / (N * (N - 1)):.1f}%")
row("raw pixels (4 grey levels)", lev[:N].astype(float))
pca = PCA(50).fit(X[:N]); Z50 = pca.transform(X[:N])
print("  top 5 variances of the PCA:", np.round(pca.explained_variance_[:5], 3))
for k in (2, 10, 50): row(f"PCA, {k} components", Z50[:, :k])
U = umap.UMAP(n_neighbors=15, random_state=42).fit_transform(Z50); row("UMAP (umap-learn) of the 50 PCA components", U)
lda = LinearDiscriminantAnalysis(n_components=9).fit(pca.transform(X[1000:5000]), yall[1000:5000]); ZL = lda.transform(Z50)
row("discriminant analysis, 2 directions", ZL[:, :2]); row("discriminant analysis, 9 directions", ZL)

10. Attention as Nadaraya–Watson (§3.2, Lab 10)

"""Lab 10 (p. 60-62): attention as Nadaraya-Watson with the kernel exp(gamma x.y), on the toy data of the author's script
Lecture_4_deep_learning/code/regression.py (whose output for gamma = 50 is the figure of p. 62), against a Gaussian kernel."""
import numpy as np
from sklearn.datasets import make_regression
from sklearn.preprocessing import MinMaxScaler
from scipy.spatial import ConvexHull

X1 = (np.array([1.0, 1.4, 2.0, 2.3, 2.9, 4.0, 4.5, 5.0, 5.4]) / 6 - 0.5)[:, None]; y1 = np.array([1.5, 0.8, 0.7, 0.2, 0.42, 1.0, 1.4, 1.1, 1.9]) / 6 - 0.25
X, y = make_regression(n_samples=20, n_features=2, noise=100, random_state=0)
X2 = MinMaxScaler((-0.4, 0.4)).fit_transform(X); y2 = MinMaxScaler((-1, 1)).fit_transform(y.reshape(-1, 1)).ravel()
def nw(Q, X, y, g, kind):
    L = g * Q @ X.T if kind == "dot" else -g * ((Q[:, None] - X[None]) ** 2).sum(-1) / 2
    W = np.exp(L - L.max(1, keepdims=True)); W /= W.sum(1, keepdims=True); return W @ y, W
author = {"1D": [0.06883956897097335, 0.06754605748786248, 0.06407187534330021, 0.06180346380246571, 0.05945097066273646, 0.07031556559979116,
                 0.08381189031212533, 0.09571565524685095, 0.10422797119951395, 0.10841242728714352],
          "2D": [0.3352583972487924, 0.3304719357646347, 0.31451139474962175, 0.28723314675671363, 0.23122936439163672, 0.24789208157013273,
                 0.31596336770553773, 0.3924470677152153, 0.4508295604245399, 0.4607191804385008]}   # printed by the author's script
G = [1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000]
for name, (Xd, yd) in [("1D", (X1, y1)), ("2D", (X2, y2))]:
    dot = [np.abs(nw(Xd, Xd, yd, g, "dot")[0] - yd).mean() for g in G]; gau = [np.abs(nw(Xd, Xd, yd, g, "gauss")[0] - yd).mean() for g in G]
    print(f"{name}: mean |prediction - y| at the training points, gamma = {G}")
    print("  exp(g x.y) :", " ".join(f"{v:.4f}" for v in dot), f"  (max |difference with the author's prints| {max(abs(a - b) for a, b in zip(dot, author[name])):.1e})")
    print("  Gaussian   :", " ".join(f"{v:.4f}" for v in gau))
u = np.linspace(-0.5, 0.5, 201); Q = np.array([[a, b] for b in u for a in u]); nn = ((Q[:, None] - X2[None]) ** 2).sum(-1).argmin(1)
for g in (5, 50, 1000):
    _, Wd = nw(Q, X2, y2, g, "dot"); _, Wg = nw(Q, X2, y2, g, "gauss")
    print(f"gamma = {g:4d}: heaviest weight on the nearest point {100 * (Wd.argmax(1) == nn).mean():.1f}% (Gaussian {100 * (Wg.argmax(1) == nn).mean():.1f}%), "
          f"median effective number of points {np.median(1 / (Wd ** 2).sum(1)):.2f} (Gaussian {np.median(1 / (Wg ** 2).sum(1)):.2f}), "
          f"key bias exp(g|x_j|^2/2) from {np.exp(g * (X2 ** 2).sum(1) / 2).min():.3g} to {np.exp(g * (X2 ** 2).sum(1) / 2).max():.3g}")
Qn = Q[(Q != 0).any(1)]
print("points that win as gamma -> infinity:", sorted(map(int, set((Qn @ X2.T).argmax(1)))), "; convex hull:", sorted(map(int, ConvexHull(X2).vertices)))

11. Extrapolating the cannonball (§3.3, Lab 11)

"""Lab 11 (p. 47, 65): extrapolating the cannonball of p. 65 (dots digitised from images/gravity.png) with a ReLU network,
a Gaussian kernel ridge, a parabola and a parabola + ReLU correction. The ReLU network is the page's own code, ported line by line
(same initialisation from the page's random generator, same L-BFGS), so that the numbers are the page's."""
import math, numpy as np
from gda_rng import Rng

dots = [(208, 86), (262, 124), (316, 154), (369.8, 177), (424, 193), (478, 200), (532, 201), (586.2, 193), (640, 178), (693, 156)]  # (x px, height px)
x0, x1 = dots[0][0], dots[-1][0]
def data(kind="cannon", noise=0, seed=3):
    r, out = Rng(seed), []
    for i, (px, h) in enumerate(dots):
        x = (px - x0) / (x1 - x0); y = 40 * math.exp(2.4 * x) if kind == "growth" else h
        out.append((x, y + (noise * r.normal() if i < len(dots) - 1 and noise else 0)))
    return out
# ---- the page's ReLU network: sizes [1, 20, 20, 1], Glorot-uniform initialisation, loss mean((f - y)^2) / 2, L-BFGS ----
def layout(sizes):
    offs, p = [], 0
    for l in range(len(sizes) - 1): offs.append((p, p + sizes[l] * sizes[l + 1], sizes[l], sizes[l + 1])); p += sizes[l] * sizes[l + 1] + sizes[l + 1]
    return offs, p
def init(sizes, rng):
    offs, n = layout(sizes); th = [0.0] * n
    for W, b, fi, fo in offs:
        bound = math.sqrt(6 / (fi + fo))
        for k in range(fi * fo): th[W + k] = rng.range(-bound, bound)
        for k in range(fo): th[b + k] = rng.range(-bound, bound)
    return th
def loss_grad(th, sizes, X, y, g=None):
    offs, _ = layout(sizes); L = len(offs); n = len(y); acts, zs = [X], []
    for l, (W, b, fi, fo) in enumerate(offs):
        A = acts[l]; Z = [0.0] * (n * fo)
        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(fo):
                s = th[b + j]
                for k in range(fi): s += A[i * fi + k] * th[W + k * fo + j]
                Z[i * fo + j] = s
        zs.append(Z)
        if l < L - 1: acts.append([v if v > 0 else 0.0 for v in Z])
    out = zs[-1]; loss = 0.0; delta = [0.0] * n
    for i in range(n): r = out[i] - y[i]; loss += r * r; delta[i] = r / n
    loss /= 2 * n
    if g is None: return loss
    for q in range(len(g)): g[q] = 0.0
    for l in range(L - 1, -1, -1):
        W, b, fi, fo = offs[l]; A = acts[l]
        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(fo):
                dv = delta[i * fo + j]
                if dv == 0: continue
                g[b + j] += dv
                for k in range(fi): g[W + k * fo + j] += A[i * fi + k] * dv
        if l > 0:
            Zp = zs[l - 1]; nd = [0.0] * (n * fi)
            for i in range(n):
                for k in range(fi):
                    if Zp[i * fi + k] <= 0: continue
                    s2 = 0.0
                    for j in range(fo): s2 += th[W + k * fo + j] * delta[i * fo + j]
                    nd[i * fi + k] = s2
            delta = nd
    return loss
def dot(a, b):
    s = 0.0
    for u, v in zip(a, b): s += u * v
    return s
def lbfgs(fg, x0, maxIter=2000, gtol=1e-7, m=10, ftol=2.220446049250313e-9):   # two-loop recursion, strong-Wolfe line search (as the page)
    n = len(x0); x = list(x0); g = [0.0] * n; f = fg(x, g); S, Y, RHO = [], [], []; alph = [0.0] * m
    for it in range(maxIter):
        if max(abs(v) for v in g) <= gtol: break
        d = [-v for v in g]; k = len(S)
        for j in range(k - 1, -1, -1):
            alph[j] = RHO[j] * dot(S[j], d); d = [di - alph[j] * yi for di, yi in zip(d, Y[j])]
        if k > 0: gam = dot(S[k - 1], Y[k - 1]) / dot(Y[k - 1], Y[k - 1]); d = [di * gam for di in d]
        else:
            gn1 = 0.0
            for v in g: gn1 += abs(v)
            sc = min(1, 1 / gn1); d = [di * sc for di in d]
        for j in range(k):
            bb = RHO[j] * dot(Y[j], d); d = [di + si * (alph[j] - bb) for di, si in zip(d, S[j])]
        dg0 = dot(g, d)
        if not dg0 < 0: S, Y, RHO = [], [], []; d = [-v for v in g]; dg0 = dot(g, d)
        c1, c2, t, tPrev, fPrev, dgPrev, tLo, tHi, fLo, dgLo, found, zoom, fnew = 1e-4, 0.9, 1.0, 0.0, f, dg0, 0.0, 0.0, f, dg0, False, False, f
        gn = [0.0] * n
        for ls in range(30):
            if zoom: t = (tLo + tHi) / 2
            xn = [xi + t * di for xi, di in zip(x, d)]; fnew = fg(xn, gn); dgt = dot(gn, d)
            if not zoom:
                if fnew > f + c1 * t * dg0 or (ls > 0 and fnew >= fPrev): zoom = True; tLo, fLo, dgLo, tHi = tPrev, fPrev, dgPrev, t; continue
                if abs(dgt) <= -c2 * dg0: found = True; break
                if dgt >= 0: zoom = True; tLo, fLo, dgLo, tHi = t, fnew, dgt, tPrev; continue
                tPrev, fPrev, dgPrev = t, fnew, dgt; t *= 2
            else:
                if fnew > f + c1 * t * dg0 or fnew >= fLo: tHi = t
                else:
                    if abs(dgt) <= -c2 * dg0: found = True; break
                    if dgt * (tHi - tLo) >= 0: tHi = tLo
                    tLo, fLo, dgLo = t, fnew, dgt
                if abs(tHi - tLo) < 1e-16: break
        if not found:
            if zoom and fLo < f and tLo > 0: t = tLo; xn = [xi + t * di for xi, di in zip(x, d)]; fnew = fg(xn, gn)
            elif not fnew < f: break
        s = [a - b for a, b in zip(xn, x)]; yv = [a - b for a, b in zip(gn, g)]; sy = dot(s, yv)
        fold = f; f = fnew; x = list(xn); g = list(gn)
        if sy > 1e-10 * dot(yv, yv):
            S.append(s); Y.append(yv); RHO.append(1 / sy)
            if len(S) > m: S.pop(0); Y.pop(0); RHO.pop(0)
        if (fold - f) / max(abs(fold), abs(f), 1) <= ftol: break
    return x
def relu_net(xs, ys, seed=1):
    sizes = [1, 20, 20, 1]; th = lbfgs(lambda t, g: loss_grad(t, sizes, xs, ys, g), init(sizes, Rng(seed)))
    return lambda x: loss_grad_predict(th, sizes, x)
def loss_grad_predict(th, sizes, x):
    offs, _ = layout(sizes); A = [x]
    for l, (W, b, fi, fo) in enumerate(offs):
        Z = []
        for j in range(fo):
            s = th[b + j]
            for k in range(fi): s += A[k] * th[W + k * fo + j]
            Z.append(0.0 if (l < len(offs) - 1 and s < 0) else s)
        A = Z
    return A[0]
def lstsq_qr(A, b):   # Householder least squares, as the page's G.lstsqQR (same operations, same rounding)
    m, p = len(A), len(A[0]); R = [row[:] for row in A]; y = list(b)
    for k in range(p):
        nrm = math.sqrt(sum(R[i][k] ** 2 for i in range(k, m)))
        if nrm == 0: continue
        alpha = -nrm if R[k][k] > 0 else nrm; v = [0.0] * m; v[k] = R[k][k] - alpha
        for i in range(k + 1, m): v[i] = R[i][k]
        vv = 0.0
        for i in range(k, m): vv += v[i] * v[i]
        if vv == 0: continue
        for j in range(k, p):
            t = 0.0
            for i in range(k, m): t += v[i] * R[i][j]
            t = 2 * t / vv
            for i in range(k, m): R[i][j] -= t * v[i]
        t = 0.0
        for i in range(k, m): t += v[i] * y[i]
        t = 2 * t / vv
        for i in range(k, m): y[i] -= t * v[i]
    x = [0.0] * p
    for k in range(p - 1, -1, -1):
        t = y[k]
        for j in range(k + 1, p): t -= R[k][j] * x[j]
        x[k] = t / R[k][k]
    return x
def variance(v):   # population variance, two passes (as the page's G.variance)
    mu = 0.0
    for a in v: mu += a
    mu /= len(v); s = 0.0
    for a in v: s += (a - mu) * (a - mu)
    return s / len(v)
def fit(pts, m, model):
    xs = [p[0] for p in pts[:m]]; ys = [p[1] for p in pts[:m]]; mu = sum(ys) / m; sd = math.sqrt(variance(ys)) or 1
    if model in ("poly2", "hybrid", "loglin"):
        deg = 1 if model == "loglin" else 2
        c = lstsq_qr([[x ** k for k in range(deg + 1)] for x in xs], [math.log(v) for v in ys] if model == "loglin" else ys)
        def base(x):
            s = 0.0
            for k in range(deg + 1): s += c[k] * x ** k
            return math.exp(s) if model == "loglin" else s
        if model != "hybrid": return base
        res = [v - base(u) for u, v in zip(xs, ys)]; rs = math.sqrt(variance(res)) or 1
        net = relu_net(xs, [r / rs for r in res]); return lambda x: base(x) + rs * net(x)
    if model == "relu":
        net = relu_net(xs, [(v - mu) / sd for v in ys]); return lambda x: mu + sd * net(x)
    K = np.exp(-np.subtract.outer(xs, xs) ** 2 / (2 * 0.15 ** 2)) + 1e-3 * np.eye(m); a = np.linalg.solve(K, np.array(ys) - mu)   # kernel ridge
    return lambda x: mu + a @ np.exp(-(x - np.array(xs)) ** 2 / (2 * 0.15 ** 2))
names = {"relu": "ReLU network 2 x 20", "kernel": "Gaussian kernel ridge", "poly2": "parabola", "hybrid": "parabola + ReLU", "loglin": "exponential"}
for kind, noise, ms in [("cannon", 0, (4, 6, 7, 8, 9)), ("growth", 0, (6,)), ("cannon", 5, (6, 8)), ("cannon", 2, (5,))]:
    pts = data(kind, noise)
    for m in ms:
        row = []
        for model in (["relu", "kernel", "poly2", "hybrid"] if kind == "cannon" else ["relu", "kernel", "loglin"]):
            f = fit(pts, m, model); row.append(f"{names[model]} {f(pts[-1][0]) - pts[-1][1]:+.1f}")
        print(f"{kind}, noise {noise} px, {m} dots seen: error at the target: " + ", ".join(row))

Exercises and mini-projects

  1. (§1.1) Counting parameters. A layer maps a 54 × 54 image with 16 channels to 54 × 54 × 16. Count the parameters of a fully connected layer, of a 5 × 5 convolution, and of a vanilla message-passing layer x ← W1x + W2 Σneighbours x on the 4-neighbour grid.
  2. (§1.2) Symmetric filters are even. Show that a 5 × 5 kernel invariant under the eight symmetries of the square satisfies φ[−k, −l] = φ[k, l], and deduce that its response to an image and to the image turned by 180° are turned copies of each other. Why does this rule out edge detectors like filter 5? (Lab 1)
  3. (§1.2) What L layers can see. Show that L layers of the sum over the 4 neighbours produce a linear combination of the rings of graph distance ≤ L, with weights given by numbers of paths. Compute these weights for L = 2.
  4. (§1.3) Coarsening. Apply the heavy-edge matching of Lab 4 by hand to a cycle of 8 vertices and to a star with 6 leaves. What happens to a star, and why is that bad for pooling?
  5. (§1.4) Indices. Compute the index of the zeros of the planar fields (x, y), (−y, x), (x, −y) and (x² − y², 2xy). Which one is the “dipole” of Lab 2 seen through a stereographic projection?
  6. (§1.4) Combing a torus. Write a tangent vector field without zeros on the torus of radii R and r. Why does this not contradict the hairy ball theorem? What is the Euler characteristic of a sphere with g handles, and how many zeros (counted with index) must a field on it have?
  7. (§1.5) The cotangent formula. Show that for a function that is linear on each triangle, the Dirichlet energy ½∫|∇u|² equals ½ Σedges ½(cot αij + cot βij)(ui − uj)², where αij, βij are the angles opposite the edge.
  8. (§1.5) Calibrating message passing. On the triangular lattice of spacing h, show that the mean over the 6 neighbours minus the centre value is (h²/4) Δu + O(h⁴). Deduce the number of steps K with τ = 0.5 used in Lab 3, and predict the spread of the heat on the graded mesh.
  9. (§1.6) Over-squashing on a path. For a path of n vertices, compute (ÂL)1n for the normalised adjacency with self-loops when L = n − 1. How fast does it decay with n?
  10. (§1.6) Curvature of a bridge. Two cliques of m vertices are joined by one edge. Compute the Ollivier–Ricci curvature of the bridge with the closed-ball measures, and its limit as m grows.
  11. (§1.7) Sectors. A warp of 32 threads reads 32 floats at random positions of an array of 106 floats. What is the expected number of distinct 32-byte sectors? With 16 floats per vertex? Compare with Lab 5.
  12. (§1.9) The K-NN curve. The error of the 1-NN vote on MNIST falls from 38.4% (50 images) to 8.0% (5,000 images) in Lab 6. Fit a power law error ≈ a n−b and extrapolate to 60,000 images; compare with 3.09%.
  13. (§1.9) Taken out of context. Design a version of the FAUST task of p. 38 that cannot be solved by memorising the template: what must change in the input (sampling, topology, noise) and in the evaluation?
  14. (§2.1) The smooth distance. Show that the soft minimum −σ log Σk exp(−dk/σ) lies between mink dk − σ log N and mink dk, and compute its gradient. What happens to the level set as σ → 0?
  15. (§2.1) Invariance. Explain why the curvatures of Lab 7 are invariant to rotations and translations of the atoms, while the correlation after a rotation is only 0.98. Which step of the pipeline is not invariant?
  16. (§2.3) Unbalanced transport. For two Dirac masses a δx and b δy, minimise ½ |x − y|² π + ρ KL(π | a) + ρ KL(π | b) over the transported mass π. When is it better to transport nothing?
  17. (§2.4) Reading a table. Using the table of p. 55 (in Lab 8), find a pair of rows that differ only by the number of points, and a pair that differ only by the method. Which effect is larger?
  18. (§3.2) Attention and Gaussians. Prove the factorisation exp(γ q · k) = exp(γ|q|²/2) exp(−γ|q − k|²/2) exp(γ|k|²/2). Show that when all keys have the same norm, softmax attention is a Gaussian Nadaraya–Watson estimator, and find which key wins as γ → ∞ in general.
  19. (§3.3) Extrapolating with ReLUs. Show that any network built from linear layers and ReLUs is piecewise linear in its input, hence linear beyond the last breakpoint. What does that imply for a parabola, and for an exponential?
  20. (Mini-project) A fair Graph-MNIST. Using the superpixel images of Lab 6, train a small graph network (e.g. two GCN layers and a mean readout) on 5,000 images, and compare it with the 1-NN vote on the same images and with an MLP that ignores the edges. Report all three with the same training data.

Cheat sheet

Convolution vs message passing (§1.1–1.2)

Grid: x[i,j] ← Σk,l φ[k,l] x[i−k, j−l], a weight per offset. Graph: x[i] ← Σi↔k φ(x[i], x[k], edge[i,k]). A convolution is message passing with the offset as edge feature. Without edge features, filters are isotropic: blurs yes, oriented edges no.

Five problems (§1.4–1.7)

1. No orientation (hairy ball: every tangent field on a sphere has zeros; indices sum to χ = 2). 2. Sampling: a graph layer ignores lengths and areas; use cotangent weights and masses. 3. Cliques cannot be pooled; bridges over-squash. 4. GPUs: scattered, uneven reads. 5. Too many kinds of data.

Over-squashing (§1.6)

Sensitivity of vertex i to vertex j after L linear GCN layers = (ÂL)ij, Â = D̃−½(A + I)D̃−½. Small across very negatively curved edges (Ollivier–Ricci). Fix: add edges around them (rewiring).

Memory (§1.7)

A warp = 32 threads; memory served in 32-byte sectors. Contiguous reads: few sectors. Random gathers: up to 32 per read. Store nearby vertices together (sort along a Z-order curve), give each vertex many features, balance the degrees.

Baselines (§1.8–1.9)

Graph-MNIST: GCN 90.1%, MLP without edges 95.3%, best graph networks 97.3%; 1-NN on raw pixels 96.9% (60,000 images), 92.0% with 5,000. FAUST on PyG: memorising one triangulation, not registration.

dMaSIF (§2.1)

Surface = level set 1.05 Å of a smooth distance to the atoms; sample by gradient steps; 1 Å cells; normals = gradient; curvatures from a local fit of how normals turn, at scales 1–10 Å. Rotation-invariant features; built on the fly, differentiable; ×459 faster than MaSIF including pre-processing.

Optimal transport registration (§2.3–2.4)

min Σ πij |xi − yj|²/2 with fixed marginals: global matching. Sinkhorn: blur ε, log domain, ε-scaling. Robust (unbalanced): marginal penalties of strength ρ, for missing parts and outliers. Move to the barycentre, smooth. Complete data: balanced; partial data: robust.

Learned graphs (§3.1)

DGCNN: K-NN graph of the features at every layer. Autoencoders, UMAP: K-NN graph of a low-dimensional code (a linear autoencoder = PCA). Neighbourhoods are only as good as the features (Lab 9: 78–82% same-digit neighbours).

Attention (§3.2)

q, k, v = MLPs of x; xi ← Σj softmaxj(qi · kj) vj: Nadaraya–Watson with k(x, y) = exp(x · y) = Gaussian × exp(|k|²/2) up to a factor in q. Long keys win; as γ → ∞, the key furthest along q, not the nearest.

Limits of learning everything (§3.3–3.4)

Data are expensive (50 patients = a thesis). Big models cost time, energy, maintenance. ReLU networks are piecewise linear: they interpolate, they do not extrapolate a parabola or an exponential. Physics + data-driven residuals (Rosetta) when both exist.

Self-test

1. What did Lecture 3 conclude about white noise, and why does it matter for this lecture?
“Statistics on white noise is hopeless” (p. 2): with independent features, all distances are alike in high dimension. Learning needs a low-dimensional structure; neighbourhood graphs describe it locally, and this lecture asks how to learn on them.
2. Which continuous geometries do cliques, grids and trees resemble, according to p. 4–5?
Balls with positive curvature, planes with flat curvature, and saddles with negative curvature. Lecture 3 measured it: Ollivier–Ricci curvature +1, 0 and −½, and balls that plateau, grow like r² and grow exponentially.
3. What does UMAP show, and what does it not show?
It shows neighbourhoods: points close in the picture were neighbours in the data. The sizes of clusters and the distances between them are not meaningful. It is a diagnostic tool, not a measurement.
4. Why are convolutions “cheap”?
A few shared coefficients (25 for a 5 × 5 filter) are reused at every pixel, with fixed, contiguous neighbourhoods that hardware and compilers handle optimally.
5. Write a grid convolution as message passing on a graph.
Vertices = pixels, edges = pairs within the filter’s window, edge[i, k] = the offset from i to k, message φ(x[i], x[k], edge[i, k]) = φ[offset] · x[k]. Lab 1 checks that the two computations agree exactly.
6. Why can isotropic graph filters not detect a vertical edge?
Their weights depend only on graph distance (or path counts), so they treat left and right, up and down, alike; a symmetric filter responds equally to an edge and to its mirror image and cannot compute their difference. In Lab 1 the best isotropic imitation of a derivative has R² ≤ 0.0042.
7. State the hairy ball theorem and the Poincaré–Hopf theorem.
Every continuous tangent vector field on a sphere vanishes somewhere. More generally, on a closed surface the indices of the isolated zeros of a field add up to the Euler characteristic V − E + F: 2 for a sphere, 0 for a torus (Lab 2).
8. Why does the hairy ball theorem matter for convolutions on surfaces?
Oriented filters need a reference direction at every point that varies continuously; on a sphere-like surface such a field must break down somewhere. Methods take the best over rotations (MaSIF) or transform features with the reference frame (gauge-equivariant networks).
9. Why does a vanilla graph layer depend on the sampling of a surface?
It only sees who is connected to whom. Moving the vertices without changing the triangles changes the surface but not the graph; meshing the same surface twice changes the graph but not the surface. In Lab 3, mean aggregation spreads heat 34% too far on a graded mesh.
10. What fixes the dependence on sampling in geometry processing?
Operators built from lengths, angles and areas, such as the cotangent Laplacian with a mass matrix, which discretise the Laplace–Beltrami operator of the surface itself: in Lab 3 they match the exact heat to within 0.4% on all three meshes.
11. Why is a clique hard to downsample?
It has no scale: every vertex is one step from every other. Pooling merges vertices but leaves diameter 1 at every level, so a hierarchy of pooled graphs sees nothing new (Lab 4).
12. What is over-squashing, and how does curvature detect it?
Information from many distant vertices must pass through a few edges and be squeezed into fixed-size vectors. The sensitivity (ÂL)ij collapses across edges of very negative curvature; on the graph of p. 25, the bridge has curvature −1.071 and the signal across is 30 times weaker after 4 layers.
13. Name two reasons why graphs run slowly on GPUs.
Scattered memory reads (a warp touches many memory sectors instead of a few) and uneven degrees (threads with few neighbours wait for those with many); also no reuse of loaded data between neighbouring vertices.
14. How much of the memory problem can a better storage order fix?
A lot: sorting the vertices of a K-NN graph along a Z-order curve brings the sectors read per warp from 6.65 to 2.29 times the ideal and the cache misses from 77% to 0.8% (Lab 5). The unevenness of the degrees remains.
15. What does the caption of p. 35 say, and what does the table itself add?
That basic K-NN classifiers reach 95–99% on MNIST, so Graph-MNIST results are only a sanity check. The table adds that the MLP, which ignores the edges, beats every GCN variant (95.34% against 90.1–90.8%).
16. Why is the PyG version of FAUST “irrelevant to shape registration”?
All 100 meshes share one triangulation of the template, in the same vertex order and aligned, so predicting the vertex index amounts to memorising the triangulation. Real registration starts from raw scans with noise, holes, other samplings and self-contacts.
17. What prior does MaSIF build in, and which invariances does it get?
Docking depends on the surfaces: features on local geodesic patches (about 1 nm). It is invariant to 3D rotations and translations and to the protein’s interior, and local, so it cannot latch onto scattered patterns.
18. How does dMaSIF sample a surface without a mesh?
It defines a smooth distance to the atoms, throws random points around them, moves each by gradient steps onto the level set 1.05 Å, discards points trapped inside, and keeps one average point per 1 Å cube; normals are the gradient.
19. Is the “×100–×1,000 faster” of p. 46 a fair comparison?
From atoms to output, 76.2 s against 0.166 s (×459), so yes when surfaces must be recomputed (design, docking, end-to-end training). If surfaces are pre-computed once, the networks alone differ by about ×4.
20. What does Rosetta’s energy show about deep learning?
After 20 years, it is a weighted sum of physical potentials and statistical terms fitted to data: a hybrid of physics and learning, which the slide calls a “point neural network” de facto.
21. Why does optimal transport register vessel trees better than nearest neighbours?
Nearest neighbours let a whole branch collapse onto a neighbouring branch of the target. Transport constrains every target point to receive only its share of mass, so branches are matched globally (Lab 8: EPE 0.0606 against 0.0144, and 0.0086 with pre-alignment and smoothing).
22. When should one use robust (unbalanced) optimal transport?
When parts are missing or there are outliers: balanced transport must move all the mass, even onto outliers (Lab 8: EPE 0.0905 with a missing branch, worse than nearest neighbours), while robust transport can leave it (0.0424). On complete data it wastes information (0.0128 against 0.0086).
23. What does RobOT’s row of the table of p. 55 show?
With 30,000 points it beats six deep methods on all six metrics, but not the supervised PWC at 8,000 points on three of them, nor the pipelines that combine networks with RobOT. At equal resolution (8,000 points) it loses to FLOT and PWC.
24. Write attention as a Nadaraya–Watson estimator and explain why it is not a nearest-neighbour smoother.
xi ← Σj exp(qi · kj) vj / Σj exp(qi · kj). Since exp(q · k) = exp(|q|²/2) exp(−|q − k|²/2) exp(|k|²/2), long keys get extra weight; in Lab 10 the heaviest weight goes to the nearest point on only 49% of the square, and as γ grows only the 5 corners of the convex hull win.
25. Why do ReLU networks extrapolate poorly, and what helps?
They are piecewise linear, so beyond the data they continue in a straight line (Lab 11: 69.7 px off the target from 6 dots). A model with the right structure (a parabola for a cannonball, 0.3 px) extrapolates; physical models with learned residuals combine both, provided the residual is not fitting noise.
